subject: GPU pool oversubscription — immediate mitigation & exec ask
messages:
From: infra-alerts@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, sofia_ivanova@redwood.com
Date: 2028-11-01T13:12:00-07:00
Subject: [ALERT] Dedicated pool us-west-2/gpu-d-pool-7 utilization spike + 5xx rate

Automated monitoring detected a sustained headroom loss in dedicated GPU pool gpu-d-pool-7 (us-west-2) over the last 28 minutes. Key signals:
- Reserved throughput for several customers is undershooting their committed qps by 18–36%.
- Latency p95 increased from 120ms -> 620ms for Gen-2 model families.
- 5xx error rate aggregated across pool: 4.7% (threshold 0.5%).
- Top contributing tenant: quantumpay-prod (tenant id qpay-prod) — accounts for ~43% of tokens queued.

Attached: pool-telemetry-20281101.csv, error-traces-20281101.txt

Action recommended: immediate allocation of burst nodes + temporary throttling of non-reserved best-effort workloads.

---
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: sofia_ivanova@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: 2028-11-01T13:25:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: [ALERT] Dedicated pool us-west-2/gpu-d-pool-7 utilization spike + 5xx rate

Folks — forwarding the monitoring alert. Quantumpay (HW-3921) looks to be the dominant tenant right now. I’m standing up an ops bridge but need quick alignment on two points:
1) Can we authorize temporary burst capacity for gpu-d-pool-7 (expected ~+16 V100-equivalent instances) while we root cause?
2) If not, we need a customer communications plan — ETA + mitigations and a credit ask if SLO is violated.

Context: Quantumpay is on Dedicated/Reserved (monthly commit). They run a mixed workload with heavy short-sequence, high-concurrency inference calls. We’ve been tuning batching for them, but tonight there was a traffic spike from a new fraud-detection rule pipeline.

I’ll drop the bridge link in 5.

-Karthik

From: Elena Ruiz <elena@quantumpay.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, sofia_ivanova@redwood.com
Cc: ops@getquantum.ai
Date: 2028-11-01T14:03:00-07:00

Karthik / Sofia —
Our customers are seeing failed authorizations and timeouts at peak checkout. We started rolling the new fraud rule at 13:00 PT and traffic jumped ~3.8x. This was a controlled rollout but the failure rate is unacceptable. Please advise immediate mitigations. We need either short-term scaling or a rollback window.

---
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: infra-alerts@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2028-11-01T14:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: [ALERT] Dedicated pool us-west-2 — mitigation in progress

On the bridge — current short-term mitigations applied:
- Throttled five identified non-reserved tenants on the pool (reduces load ~22%).
- Enabled per-tenant KV prefix caching for quantumpay-prod for high-frequency endpoints (instant ~18% p95 reduction).
- Fallback routing policy enabled: route lower-priority inference to alternate pool in us-east-1 where headroom available.

We requested burst capacity; pending approval from infra-costs (cc: Vivek). If approved, we can add capacity within 8–12 minutes; otherwise we’ll need to extend throttling window and proceed with cross-region fallback (~120ms added latency).

Sofia
Sr. Ops Engineer

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, sofia_ivanova@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com

I’m authorizing a limited burst capacity draw against the emergency pool for up to 12 V100-equivalents for 2 hours to buy breathing room — cost center: emergency-burst. Approver: Vivek Kulkarni.

Notes / constraints:
- We cannot add more than 12 nodes without exec sign-off (CFO approval required for >$90k incremental spend).

Vivek
VP Ops & Commercial

---
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@quantumpay.com>, ops@getquantum.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, sofia_ivanova@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: 2028-11-02T09:32:00-07:00
Subject: Next steps and timeline — Quantumpay (HW-3921) production impact

Elena — thanks for the quick flag. Short summary and immediate next steps: 
1) We’ve applied emergency burst (+12 V100-eq) to gpu-d-pool-7 at 15:10 PT last night (temporary, 2 hours). That reduced p95 to ~210ms and 5xx to 0.9% during the window.
2) We throttled non-reserved tenants and activated cross-region fallback for best-effort traffic — this recovered steady-state but adds ~120ms to fallback requests.
3) We enabled per-tenant KV caching for the hot prefix in your workflow which reduced token compute by ~17% on the most common path.

Open asks from our side: 
- Can Quantumpay delay the remaining rollout batch for the fraud rule for 6 hours so we can validate the longer-term mitigation?
- We will prepare a postmortem and SLO assessment; if SLA breach confirmed, our standard remediation includes pro-rated credits and a technical RCA.

Internal follow-ups (cc’d to Sales/Ops/Leadership):
- Marissa: please coordinate customer communication and draft credit proposal if we confirm sustained SLA violation.
- Vivek: do we need exec sign-off to extend burst beyond 2 hours? If so, recommend an approval path for immediate escalation (CFO + CEO).
- Sofia: keep telemetry attached and capture the delta after rollout pause. Attachments: quantumpay-slo.pdf, pool-telemetry-20281101.csv, error-traces-20281101.txt

We’ll schedule a quick sync with Quantumpay at 11:00 PT to align.

-Karthik
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
